clue.text: 12 3 replaced? No replacement!

definitions.note: 12 across is DRUMMER, the theme word; this answer is a drummer

indicators.note: the exclamation turns replacement into an order to put these letters in new places

parts.note: 3 down is the second word of 17, WATTS
taken as written, as part of the fodder
taken as written, as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Rolling Stones' drummer was replaced, and the answer comes back firmly: no.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether Charlie Watts was replaced, but WATTS, REPLACED and NO are all fodder, rearranged into the drummer of the Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewart Copeland played the drums in the Police, so he is an example of a drummer.

clue.text: Because round leg not quite right, one's attached to arm

indicators.note: round means the word for because goes around the shortened leg

parts.note: since means because

indicators.note: not quite means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: An odd sentence about an injured leg and a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a body part next to 'leg', but it is a firearm. LEG less its final letter gives LE, which goes inside SINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A silencer is a device screwed onto the barrel of a gun, an arm in the weapons sense.

clue.text: See 17 across
First of contenders, or enemy beaten — formality

indicators.note: first of means take only the opening letter of contenders
beaten means these letters are battered into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contest where the enemy is beaten, as if the result were a mere formality.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony is a formal occasion or observance, and formality can mean such a ritual act.

clue.text: Band ultimately entering part of joint?

definitions.text: Band ultimately entering part of joint?

indicators.note: entering means the final letter goes inside the joint part

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting piece of a mortise and tenon joint in carpentry

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of band

explanation.surface: The whole clue describes the answer: a band of tissue which, cryptically, gets inside a carpentry joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a tendon is a tough band connecting muscle to bone, often at a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a fibrous band of tissue that crosses joints, joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Initially tight on artist, match kit

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of tight

parts.note: Henri Rousseau was a French painter

explanation.surface: A tight-fitting sports kit for an artist playing in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like sport, but it is a marriage; the clue's 'on' places the artist after the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride gathers for her marriage, the match.

clue.text: Diminutive figure briefly working, bit of an old timer

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a gnome is a small figure, as in a garden
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A garden gnome rushes off to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnomon is the pointer on a sundial that casts the shadow, part of an ancient clock.

clue.text: Partners after the Guardian's money entering loan, if poorly represented in time?

indicators.note: entering means the newspaper money and partners go inside the jumbled letters
poorly represented means the letters of loan, if are set out badly, in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: after means the partners come after the newspaper's money

parts.note: the newspaper speaking of itself says our
a dime is a US coin, so money
N and S, north and south, are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: A rambling sentence about the newspaper lending its money badly.
explanation.walkthrough: OURDIMENS goes into FIONAL, the anagram of LOAN IF, after the F. 'entering' is the signal for the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics treats time as a fourth dimension added to the three of space, so existing in time is having that extra dimension.

clue.text: Asian swallow flying west across India gradually disappears

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
in an across answer, flying west means read right to left

parts.note: to swallow is to eat
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
wanes means gradually disappears, like the moon

explanation.surface: A swallow migrating west over India fades into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like the bird, but it is the verb. TAE goes across I and WANES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Taiwan, an island state in East Asia, is Asian.

clue.text: OO12

parts.note: the first O is read as a ring, the second as the letter O, and 12 is DRUMMER

explanation.surface: A bare string of letters and a number, like a code.
explanation.walkthrough: An O is shaped like a ring: one O becomes RING, the other stays O, and 12 across says the result is a drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the drummer of the Beatles, so this name points to a famous drummer.

clue.text: Gales etc back towards the front — wind!

indicators.note: back towards the front means the last letter travels up towards the start of the word

parts.note: gales and the like are weather

explanation.surface: A weather forecast of gales coming back again, punctuated by a cry about the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like the noun after gales, but it is the verb, rhymed with mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreathe is to twist or coil around something, which is to wind.

clue.text: Stranger at back of band?

indicators.note: at means the last letter of band sits beside the stranger
back of means the last letter of band

parts.note: rum means strange, so rummer is stranger

explanation.surface: A curious figure lurking at the rear of a pop group, which is where the drummer sits.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the drummer sits at the back of a band. 'Stranger' looks like a noun, but it is the comparative of rum.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage a drummer usually plays behind the other members, so is found at the back of the group.

clue.text: Absurd 12

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as in 'that's ...', is laughably absurd
second meaning: Buddy ..., the American jazz drummer

explanation.definitionFit: Rich means ridiculous in the idiom 'that's rich', and Buddy Rich was a famous jazz drummer.

clue.text: Tunisian built on second peninsular peak

indicators.note: on means the anagram is placed upon the second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: built means the letters of Tunisian are constructed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tunisian builder constructs something in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: MO goes first and the anagram of TUNISIAN, UNTSINAI, is built on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai stands on the Sinai Peninsula in Egypt, so it is a peak on a peninsula.

clue.text: Picture finally framed by buddies on display behind 12

definitions.note: 12 across is DRUMMER; this is the Who's drummer

indicators.note: framed by means the letter is set inside the buddies like a picture in a frame

parts.note: kith are friends, as in kith and kin

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of picture

parts.note: to moon is to display one's bare behind

explanation.surface: A photo of friends baring their bottoms, framed for the drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a preposition, but it is the noun for the rump.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Moon played the drums for the Who, so he is an example of a drummer.

clue.text: Grant entertains retired minister in restaurant

indicators.note: entertains means holds the minister inside, as a host does a guest

parts.note: Cary Grant, the film actor

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: A film star treats a retired clergyman to a meal out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a verb, but it is the actor Cary Grant. REV turned round is VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is a restaurant where roast meat is carved to order, a British buffet-style eatery.

clue.text: 12's possible reason for high amount of power?

definitions.note: 12 across is DRUMMER; this is the Rolling Stones' drummer

parts.note: charlie is slang for cocaine, which makes a person high
watts measure electrical power

explanation.surface: Wonders why the drummer seems so energised.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is British slang for cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Watts was the Rolling Stones' drummer, so he is an example of a drummer.

clue.text: Children's author in study penning playful affair on troublemakers, primarily

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: to con is to study, an old sense

indicators.note: on means the troublemakers' letter follows the romp

parts.note: a romp is a light-hearted frolic

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of troublemakers

explanation.surface: A children's writer at a desk, writing a playful story about troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmal Crompton wrote the Just William books, about an unruly schoolboy, for young readers.

clue.text: Rule about 21 underwear

indicators.note: about means the rule goes around the 21

parts.note: to rule is to draw a line, and a ruled line is a line
21 down is GINGER: Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: A rule concerning Ginger's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is GINGER, but here it stands for the Spice Girl Geri Halliwell, known as Ginger Spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underclothing, a kind of underwear.

clue.text: Fair, fair love in the Lord

parts.note: fair means beautiful, pretty

indicators.note: in means the love goes inside the word for the Lord

parts.note: God is the Lord
love is nil, O, in tennis

explanation.surface: A devout line about fair love in the Lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair can mean reasonably good, neither poor nor excellent, which matches this phrase.

clue.text: Palace guard Newcastle United centre half after eight unbelievable headers

indicators.note: after means the club and the position follow the two headers
headers means the first letters of the words, as at the head

parts.note: NU is Newcastle United
CH is the football abbreviation for centre half

explanation.surface: A Newcastle United centre half scores eight unbelievable headed goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headers' looks like football, but it means the first letters of eight and unbelievable.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunuchs were castrated men who guarded the women's quarters of royal palaces.

clue.text: 12, one cooking something spicy?

definitions.note: 12 across is DRUMMER; this is Cream's drummer

parts.note: ginger is a spice
a baker cooks bread

explanation.surface: A drummer as a baker of spicy cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the pieces are one who bakes ginger, as in gingerbread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger Baker was the drummer of the rock band Cream, so he is an example of a drummer.

clue.text: First spent, extra cash for duty

indicators.note: first spent means the opening letter is used up and gone

parts.note: a bonus is extra pay

explanation.surface: The first thing spent is a worker's bonus, money for doing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a responsibility or obligation, which is a duty.

clue.text: See 21
TV connector, zero switches, piece behind back of clock

indicators.note: behind means the piece comes after the clock's letter
switches means the word turns round, the letters swapped end to end

parts.note: nil is zero

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of clock

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Fixing a TV: wiring at zero, switches flicked, a part fitted behind a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: NIL turned round is LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkman is a presenter who joins the items of a broadcast programme, so connects TV segments.

clue.text: Opponent originally chasing tie in lead — which has no real effect

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the letter follows
in means the tie goes inside the lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
to lace is to tie

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of opponent

explanation.surface: In a football tie, an opponent comes from behind to chase a team leading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like being ahead, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active ingredient, given for its psychological rather than medical effect.

clue.text: Mixture of hot and cold on a chip

indicators.note: mixture of means these letters are stirred together

parts.note: H stands for hot, on a tap
C stands for cold, on a tap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dip of hot and cold sauces served on a chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served topped with cheese.

clue.text: I create works including very specialised stuff

indicators.note: including means the scrambled letters take very inside them
works means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: An artist boasts of creating very specialised works.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I CREATE is ETERICA, and SO goes after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure items or knowledge of interest only to a select few.
